chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:

I said to him, 'A man missed a prayer from the travel prayer and remembered it during residence.' He said, 'He should make up what he missed as it was missed. If it was the travel prayer, he performs it during residence like it [shortened]. And if it was the residence prayer, he should make up the residence prayer during travel.'

key_terms.فَاتَتْهُ: It missed him / he missed it
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up / performs the makeup prayer

ai.seo_question: How should a traveler make up a missed prayer if they return home before praying it?
ai.summary: This narration from Zurara, a key figure in early Shia jurisprudence, clarifies the principle of 'preservation of the original state' (ithbat al-hal) in qada, ensuring that the ritual integrity of the missed prayer is maintained regardless of the worshipper's current location. It establishes a practical legal precedent in the Tusi school, distinguishing between the obligation to shorten (qasr) or complete (tamam) the makeup based on the state during the original missed time rather than the time of repayment.
